trap-negation-contrast.evidence: 'If the electron cloud is not a union of closed sub-links, then at least one trefoil contains an available linking site' is a contrapositive step in an iff proof, not an assert-by-denying construction.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: pass on all ten trap criteria. THREE FINDINGS, none fixed inline. (1) A PROPOSITION PROVED FROM A CONJECTURE, invisible to the manifest. The reverse direction says in so many words 'follows from the shell conjecture'. The natural referent in the corpus is conj:electron-shell-2n2-capacity. Neither this proof's uses[] (['prop:noble-gas-characterization']) nor the proposition's uses[] (['rem:helium-hopf-diagram']) declares any conj: label, so the conjectural-propagation audit of AGENTS.md 3b cannot see the dependency — and 3b requires a block downstream of a conjecture to be a conjecture, or to satisfy the 3b-cond conditional-class exception with the conjecture named in uses[] and carried as an explicit instance hypothesis. Neither holds here. Proposed: name the conjecture with a link, add it to uses[], and either demote the proposition or state it conditionally. (2) UNRESOLVED CITATION: 'the Hopf stability proposition' is given without a label. The only Hopf-stability result in the corpus is prop:torus-hopf-stability, 'Torus knot composites on Bring's surface are stable hadrons' — a statement about HADRONS, not about electron sub-Hopf links, so either the citation points somewhere else or the domains do not match. (3) THE REVERSE DIRECTION'S PHYSICAL STEP IS FALSE AS STATED: 'The atom lowers its energy by capturing an additional electron, contradicting chemical inertness.' An open linking site does not imply a favourable electron capture — nitrogen, magnesium and manganese all have unfilled shells and non-positive electron affinity, and alkali metals react by donating rather than capturing. The argument needs 'gains or loses an electron', or a restriction to atoms with positive electron affinity.
